items.headline: Indian Ocean quake poses no tsunami risk
items.summary: A magnitude 6.5 earthquake struck the Mauritius–Réunion region of the Indian Ocean at 4:36 PM at a depth of 10 km. Authorities said there is no tsunami threat and Sri Lanka's coasts are safe.

items.headline: Amber landslide alert for Kandy, Kegalle
items.summary: The NBRO issued an Amber landslide warning for seven divisional areas in Kandy and Kegalle until 4 PM Wednesday after over 100 mm of rain in 24 hours, with Yellow alerts for other parts of both districts. Residents are told to be ready to evacuate.

items.headline: Travellers may fly without ETA for now
items.summary: With the ETA website down for maintenance, Immigration is letting eligible foreign visitors board flights without prior ETA approval until further notice. Nationals of seven countries, including Pakistan, Nigeria and Afghanistan, are excluded.

items.headline: China to help upgrade Sri Lanka Police
items.summary: An agreement signed at Police Headquarters commits China to train officers on tech-enabled crime and upgrade police infrastructure. It was signed by the Chinese Ambassador and the Public Security Ministry Secretary.

items.headline: Police SI gets 50 years for abusing schoolgirl
items.summary: A police Sub-Inspector was sentenced to 50 years' rigorous imprisonment over the abduction and sexual abuse of a schoolgirl, in a case heard at the Kurunegala High Court.

items.headline: Ravi K questions inflation and money printing
items.summary: Opposition MP Ravi Karunanayake asked how inflation is rising if the government is not printing money. He urged the Central Bank to give accurate projections and a stabilisation plan.

items.headline: New Puttalam District Secretariat complex
items.summary: Cabinet approved a four-storey office block, a 1,000-seat auditorium and parking at the current Puttalam DS site. Offices are now scattered because only part of a 2013 plan was built.

items.headline: Indian Coast Guard ship in Trincomalee
items.summary: The Indian Coast Guard ship Sujay is in Trincomalee until November 25 to support a joint India–Sri Lanka cycling expedition. Its crew is also training Sri Lankan coast guards on pollution-response equipment.

items.headline: Heavy showers forecast for several provinces
items.summary: The Met Department expects showers and thundershowers across much of the island, with over 75 mm possible in parts of the Western, Sabaragamuwa, Central, Uva and North Western provinces and Galle and Matara. People are warned about strong winds and lightning.

items.headline: SL women climb ICC T20I rankings
items.summary: Vishmi Gunaratne jumped 37 places to 51st among batters and Imesha Dulani rose to 23rd. In bowling, Kavisha Dilhari moved to 12th and Sugandika Kumari to 13th.

items.headline: Sooryavanshi, 15, hits record 204 off 53
items.summary: India A's Vaibhav Sooryavanshi set List A records with a 28-ball hundred, a 52-ball double century and 28 sixes against the UAE in Doha. India A won by seven wickets.
